subject: FinServCo: SOC 2 evidence request — SDLC credential custody & CI/CD controls
messages:
From: Elisa Park <elisa.park@finservco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: FinServCo SDLC evidence ask — code review / CI controls / secrets

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this on. We are running a SOC 2 assessment and the assessor has asked for evidence around your Secure SDLC relevant to our integration. Specifically they want:

- A short mapping of how code review is enforced (branch/protection rules, mandatory reviews, PR checks)
- The CI/CD control matrix (who can trigger deployments, approval gates, RBAC for pipelines)
- Secrets management and rotation approach (where credentials are stored, rotation cadence, emergency rotation)
- Change management / emergency patch chronology for the last 6 months for services that serve FinServCo data

Would you be able to provide a package that includes: a one-page summary, sampled artifacts (CI logs, PR history excerpts), and any runbooks for secret rotation? Our assessor would like the materials by EOD April 4.

Appreciate it — let me know if you need more time.

Best,
Elisa Park
Senior Security Analyst — FinServCo
attachments: none
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: security+questionnaire@finservco.com
Date: 2028-04-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo SDLC evidence ask — code review / CI controls / secrets

Hi Elisa — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver everything requested; rough plan below and initial artifacts attached.

Summary of what I attached (see attachments and Drive link below):
- redwood_sdlc_summary.pdf — one-page overview focused on code review, pipeline RBAC, and change governance
- redwood_ci_cd_control_matrix.csv — matrix showing pipeline roles, approval gates, and audit log locations
- secret_rotation_playbook.md — procedures for rotation and emergency revocation (includes rotation cadence)
- sdlc_change_log_excerpt.csv — filtered change log for services in scope (last 6 months)

Quick answers:
- Code review: enforced via protected branches (require 2 approvers for release branches), automated checks (lint/test/security scans) block merges. We keep PR review timestamps and reviewer IDs in the PR history exported as part of the artifact set.
- CI/CD: deployment pipelines require an approvals job for production; deploy access is role-bound to engineering leads and SREs; all pipeline runs are logged to our audit bucket with immutable timestamps.
- Secrets: we use a managed KMS + secrets store (customer-managed keys for Private deployments) with 90-day rotation by default; emergency rotation runbook included.
- Change mgmt: we keep a changelog and a change request ticket reference in each deploy; the excerpt includes approved change requests and rollbacks.

I included a Drive folder with the artifacts and a short runbook. If you'd like, I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with our SRE to go over the rotation playbook and CI gating.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-sdlc-runbook
Attachments: redwood_sdlc_summary.pdf, redwood_ci_cd_control_matrix.csv, secret_rotation_playbook.md, sdlc_change_log_excerpt.csv

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-04-02T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo SDLC evidence ask — code review / CI controls / secrets

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. I pulled the summary and the playbook. A couple of follow-ups from the assessor: 

1) For secrets: can you confirm whether rotation is automated end-to-end, or if there is any manual step that requires human action (and if so, who is authorized)?
2) For the CI/CD control matrix: we need an example pipeline run log showing an approval step and the associated user identity for a production deploy (redacted for PII is okay).
3) For change mgmt: the assessor wants the change request tickets that map to the sampled deploys you provided (ticket IDs are fine; links preferred).

Would it be possible to get these three items by EOD April 3? If anything is sensitive, point us to the redacted copy or the audit bucket location.

Elisa
